title: Resource-Oriented API Design
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of resource-oriented api design in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to choosing resource names.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers resource-oriented api design within api design, versioning, and integration. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use resource-oriented api design to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is predictable client-server contracts, resource naming, typed parameters and correct HTTP semantics.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Resource-Oriented API Design matters because it is part of api design, versioning, and integration. In practice, focus on predictable client-server contracts, resource naming, typed parameters and correct HTTP semantics. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “Choosing resource names”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “Resource-Oriented API Design”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “Choosing resource names” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Resource-Oriented API Design, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.

summary: Resource-Oriented API Design belongs to the broader goal of predictable client-server contracts, resource naming, typed parameters and correct HTTP semantics.
